sample_unit: consecutively treated patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (prospective validation)
models_evaluated: deep-learning-based automated radiotherapy planning model (4 iterative versions)

links.outcome: AI plan dosimetric quality across development center and 4 external centers
links.effect: In the 5-center retrospective evaluation (125 development-center and 120 external-center patients), AI-generated plans achieved superior or comparable dosimetric quality relative to expert manual plans despite variations in imaging, contouring, and prescription practices.
links.quote: In the 5-center retrospective evaluation, artificial intelligence (AI)-generated plans achieved superior or comparable dosimetric quality relative to expert manual plans, despite variations in imaging, contouring, and prescription practices.

links.outcome: AI-generated plan quality compared with expert manual plans on same patients
links.effect: AI plans achieved superior or comparable dosimetric quality relative to expert manual plans in a 5-center retrospective benchmark.
links.quote: In the 5-center retrospective evaluation, artificial intelligence (AI)-generated plans achieved superior or comparable dosimetric quality relative to expert manual plans, despite variations in imaging, contouring, and prescription practices.

screen.reason: The study prospective validates a deep-learning-based automated radiotherapy treatment planning system in a clinical workflow, assessing clinical acceptance and delivery quality without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice comparison.
